comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C70-C73 regarding homoeolog expression loss in three outlier individuals and the inference of chromosome 3 loss/replacement. Both evaluations find these claims supported by the data.

Strong agreement on claims C57-C67, C81-C82 regarding HEB analysis and homoeologous synapsis evidence. Both find the findings supported, though peer reviewers note the analysis was 'limited by the difficulty of inferring homeologous recombination breakpoints with RNAseq data.' OpenEval does not include C68 in this result, which peer reviewers address separately.

Strong agreement on claims C47-C54, C80, C90-C91 regarding ELD patterns and the two-phase model. Both evaluations find these claims supported and view them as effectively demonstrating short- and long-term contributions to expression evolution.

Agreement on claims C74-C76 regarding homoeolog expression changes and mechanistic interpretations. Both find these claims supported as part of understanding mechanisms driving gene expression variation in allopolyploids. OpenEval does not include C92 in this result.

Agreement on claims C55-C56, C93 regarding TRE patterns. Both find these claims supported as demonstrating long-term evolutionary changes. OpenEval includes C93 (literature context), while peer review includes C78 (which OpenEval addresses in R6).

Agreement on uncertainty regarding claims C69, C83, C94-C95, C97 about homoeologous synapsis evolution and selection. Both evaluations acknowledge these as speculative with significant limitations due to RNA-seq resolution constraints. OpenEval also includes C98 as speculative, while peer review does not explicitly address it.

Strong agreement on claims C20-C29, C77, C86 regarding selfing syndrome phenotypes evolving post-allopolyploidization. Both find these claims supported and compelling. Peer review also includes seed viability claims (C30-C34) in this result, which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Agreement on claims C30-C34, C77, C87 regarding seed viability recovery. Both find these claims supported. Peer reviewers suggest minor methodological improvements (linear mixed models vs ANOVA). OpenEval includes C88-C89 (mechanistic context), which peer review does not explicitly address.

Agreement on claims C40-C45 regarding differential expression analysis. Both find these claims supported as part of the overall contribution to understanding expression evolution. OpenEval also addresses C46 (GO enrichment) in this result, which peer review addresses separately in R9.

Partial overlap on claims C35-C36, C38-C39 regarding MDS analysis and RNA-seq experimental design. Both find these claims supported. OpenEval includes additional claims about phasing analysis (C37) and data quality metrics (C99-C101) not explicitly addressed by peer reviewers.

Disagreement on claim C46 regarding GO enrichment analysis. OpenEval finds it supported but notes limited biological interpretation (only one significant term after correction). Peer reviewers view it as uncertain/insufficient and suggest expanding the analysis to explore what kinds of genes experienced different forms of expression evolution.

OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims C1-C19, C103-C104 as supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background context.

OpenEval evaluates main conclusions C84-C85 about the two-phase model as supported by multiple lines of evidence. No single corresponding peer review result, though peer reviewers affirm the overall contribution throughout their evaluation.
OpenEval evaluates claim C96 about TE content as uncertain/speculative, noting it is not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific speculative claim.
OpenEval evaluates claim C102 about self-compatibility as supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as this is background context rather than a novel finding.
